column4: Visit note | 2026-02-21 11:30 AM | Dr. Fahmida Yasmin, ENT | Patient: Jubayer Hossain, 61, male. Mr. Hossain reports that his symptoms are worse with dust, alongside itchy eyes and frequent sneezing fits. He explains that his condition flares each spring in Lalbagh. He works as a photographer, which exposes him to outdoor dust and bright environments. He reports about 14 sneezing fits a day. He has no other major comorbidity. He denies fever, facial pain, or hearing loss. On examination: about 14 sneezing fits a day, BP 127/82 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, weight 80 kg. Nasal mucosa appears pale with clear secretions. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no medicine needed at this stage; no new medicine was prescribed and no prescription was issued today. He was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash bedding weekly. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2026-02-24 04:00 PM | Dr. Saiful Alam, Endocrinology | Patient: Rupa Bhuiyan, 58, female. Mrs. Bhuiyan states she feels constant low energy and aching bones. She mentions this began after months of night shifts indoors in Banani. She works as a CNG auto-rickshaw driver, managing long hours on the road. She has a known comorbidity of Hypothyroidism. She reports taking her thyroid medication regularly and denies severe joint swelling or acute distress. On examination: vitamin D level 12 ng/mL, BP 127/86 mmHg, pulse 84 bpm, weight 53 kg. Systemic examination is unremarkable apart from mild generalized muscle tenderness. Assessment: Vitamin D deficiency. Plan: lifestyle and self-care advice only, no medicine needed at this stage; no new medicine was prescribed and no new prescription was issued today. She was advised to get 20 minutes of morning sunlight daily and eat eggs and fish. Follow-up in 3 months with a repeat vitamin D level.
